headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make data leakage and capability conflict plausible; prompt-injection risk is lower but nonzero via MCP/CLI content flow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata can expose content through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and an MCP server, while slim is an interactive CLI that reads files and executes commands. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if OpenMetadata outputs are copied into slim’s prompt or scripts. The pair lacks direct provenance controls in the profiles, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata outputs are pasted into slim's interactive prompt or shell commands, injection becomes actionable.
IF a shared MCP or text channel is used without provenance tagging, attacker-controlled content can steer slim.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted OpenMetadata output into slim prompts.
Require a human to retype or sanitize any instructions before execution.
Add a fixed prompt prefix that treats upstream text as data only.
Use separate terminals and logs for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels on OpenMetadata outputs before any downstream parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/trust data, and slim reads/writes filesystem artifacts plus handles certificate private keys and registry credentials. slim also has broad network egress, so if the pair shares a workspace or files, sensitive material can be exposed or exfiltrated. The profiles do not show isolation between them, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or mounted volume, sensitive metadata can flow from OpenMetadata into slim.
IF slim is pointed at directories containing keys, credentials, or governance exports, those contents can be transmitted off-host.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories with no shared mount.
Remove secrets and key files from any slim target path.
Block outbound network for slim during analysis when possible.
Use a throwaway copy of any OpenMetadata export before handing it to slim.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata can run multiple instances and uses APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP, while slim can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. If both touch the same directory or artifact set, concurrent writes and destructive transformations are plausible. Because no locking or shared-state protection is documented, uncertainty again favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or inconsistent state can occur.
IF OpenMetadata emits artifacts that slim rewrites in place, concurrent mutation can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Make shared artifacts read-only before slim runs.
Serialize runs so only one agent writes at a time.
Snapshot inputs before handing them to slim.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can produce lineage, governance, and trust outputs that slim may consume as files or command inputs, but slim is not documented here as automatically acting on OpenMetadata outputs. The pathway exists in default workflows if operators chain them, yet there is no direct evidence of blind automation. That supports medium rather than high.
conditions: IF slim consumes OpenMetadata-generated files or text without verification, upstream errors can cascade.
IF OpenMetadata emits stale lineage or governance metadata that slim uses operationally, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a manual review step between OpenMetadata and slim.
Compare OpenMetadata outputs against source-of-truth files before use.
Mark generated artifacts as untrusted in filenames or directories.
Limit slim to read-only inspection of upstream outputs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation and checksum checks before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance and memory/trust data, while slim handles certificate files, private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials. The profiles do not specify residency or certification mismatches, so a direct compliance breach is not proven. However, the combination creates a realistic retention and handling mismatch if the same sensitive data class is routed through both tools.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in OpenMetadata and then copied into slim logs or artifacts, retention controls may diverge.
IF registry credentials or private keys are processed by slim under a stricter policy than OpenMetadata, policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of slim inputs.
Redact secrets before any handoff between tools.
Review retention settings for both tools before use.
Store compliance-sensitive exports in a separate bucket or folder.
requires-engineering: align data-handling policies and audit logging across both systems.
